title: On the gonality of Kneser graphs
summary: The Kneser graphs $\text{KG}(n,k)$ are a classically studied family of graphs. One known invariant of graphs is gonality (also called divisorial gonality), which is the minimum degree of a rank 1 divisor on the graph. Using known bounds on gonality of simple, connected graphs, one may obtain that the gonality of $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is bounded above by $\binom{n-1}{k}$. In 2014, Harvey and Wood showed that the treewidth (a lower bound on gonality) for $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is $\binom{n-1}{k}-1$ for $n\geq 4k^2-3k+2$.
